# Base Image: Use a recent, stable base like Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, Python, and certificates
# - build-essential, cmake: For compiling C++ applications
# - git: To clone the LAMMPS source code repository
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries for parallel execution
# - python3, python3-dev, python3-pip: Required by the LAMMPS build system (FIX)
# - ca-certificates: To allow secure connections (e.g., for git clone)
# We clean up the apt cache in the same RUN layer to reduce the final image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    python3 \
    python3-dev \
    python3-pip \
    ca-certificates \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for container environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings prevent OpenMPI from using shared memory mechanisms that
# are not available across pods and tell it to ignore local loopback and
# docker-specific network interfaces, improving stability in clustered runs.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Define the location for the LAMMPS source code
ENV LAMMPS_SRC_DIR=/opt/lammps

# Clone the latest stable branch of the LAMMPS repository.
# A shallow clone (--depth 1) is used to reduce download size.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git ${LAMMPS_SRC_DIR}

# Build and install LAMMPS from source.
# 1. Create a build directory to keep the source tree clean.
# 2. Run cmake to configure the build. We enable MPI (BUILD_MPI) and the
#    required ReaxFF package (PKG_REAXFF). KSPACE is also enabled as it is common.
# 3. Compile using all available processor cores (`make -j$(nproc)`).
# 4. Install the 'lmp' executable to `/usr/local/bin`, which is on the system PATH.
RUN cd ${LAMMPS_SRC_DIR} && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake ../cmake \
      -D CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
      -D BUILD_MPI=on \
      -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
      -D PKG_KSPACE=on \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install

# Set the default working directory for container execution.
# This is where simulations will be run from.
WORKDIR /data

# Copy the required example input files from the cloned source into the WORKDIR.
# This prepares the container to run the 'HNS' ReaxFF example immediately.
RUN cp ${LAMMPS_SRC_DIR}/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /data/

# The 'lmp' executable is now on the system PATH, ready for use.
# Example command to run a simulation:
# mpirun -np <cores> lmp -in in.hns

  namespace: default
spec:

  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 8 -v y 8 -v z 8 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for a single-node LAMMPS experiment
# on an AWS CPU instance within a Kubernetes cluster, managed by the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job.
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  # Deploying to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Defines the size of the MiniCluster in terms of pods.
  # A size of 1 ensures the entire job runs on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job.
  # The Flux Operator will prepend `flux run -n 4` to the command.
  tasks: 4

  # When set to false, the job pods are not deleted upon completion,
  # which is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

  # Configuration for the application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # This is the main command to be executed for the simulation.
      # The Flux Operator automatically wraps this command with `flux run`.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This container is a worker, not the one that launches the MiniCluster.
      launcher: false
  
  # Defines the logging behavior for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Strict mode will cause the job to fail on any warning or error.
    strict: true

The previous attempt on a c6i.16xlarge (32 physical cores) resulted in a 46s wall time. This attempt switches to an HPC-optimized ARM instance (hpc7g.16xlarge) which offers 64 physical cores. By doubling the core count and using a specialized instance type, we expect a significant reduction in wall time.

The hpc7g.16xlarge ARM instance (28s) demonstrated a significant performance improvement over the comparable c6i.16xlarge Intel instance (46s). This is primarily due to the higher physical core count (64 vs 32), indicating the application scales well with cores. As hpc7g.16xlarge has the highest physical core count available in the list, it is considered the optimal choice.

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-mc
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 8 -v y 8 -v z 8 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    launcher: false
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
  size: 1
  tasks: 64
